about: MyDay's own word families for the Arabic starter words (1.38.0): authored and checked, never worked out automatically. Words are named by their fixed id in the curriculum package's lexicon_seed. app/scripts/validate-families.mjs checks this file at every build.

families.pattern_en: مَكْتَبَة = مَـ “place of” + ك-ت-ب “writing”. You already know this pattern: see it again in مَدْرَسَة, in the د-ر-س family.

word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-009: From the root ك-ت-ب, “writing”. The same root gives you “wrote”, “writes”, “books” and “library”.
word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-010: The plural of كِتَاب: the same root, reshaped. Arabic plurals often change a word’s shape rather than adding an ending.
word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-036: “He wrote”: the past form. Its partner يَكْتُبُ is “he writes”.
word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-037: “He writes”: the present form, which adds يَـ at the front. Its partner is كَتَبَ, “he wrote”.
word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-012: مَـ “place of” + ك-ت-ب “writing”: a place of books — a library, or a bookshop by context.

also_in_examples.note_en: “Place of writing”: the same مَـ pattern, in عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ.
The present with أَ for “I” instead of يَـ for “he”, in أَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ أَكْتُبُ.

families.pattern_en: The مَـ place pattern again: مَدْرَسَة, “place of study”. Two families, one pattern — patterns repeat more than words do.

word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-038: “He studied”: the past form. Its partner يَدْرُسُ is “he studies”.
word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-039: “He studies”: the present form, with يَـ at the front. Its partner is دَرَسَ, “he studied”.
word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-011: مَـ “place of” + د-ر-س “studying”: a place of study, a school.

also_in_examples.note_en: The present with نَـ for “we”, in نَحْنُ نَدْرُسُ.
The present with أَ for “I”, in أَدْرُسُ الْيَوْمَ.

families.pattern_en: Your third past ⇄ present pair. Three verbs, one habit: the root stays; the vowels change, and the present adds يَـ.

word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-034: “He read”: the past form — and the root the word Qurʾān is built from. Its partner يَقْرَأُ is “he reads”.
word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-035: “He reads”: the present form, with يَـ at the front. Its partner is قَرَأَ, “he read”.

also_in_examples.note_en: The present with أَ for “I”, in أَقْرَأُ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.

families.pattern_en: Not a verb pair this time — a gender pair, made with ة. The same ending as مَدْرَسَة and فِكْرَة.

word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-013: A male student: one who seeks (knowledge).
word_notes.lexeme.arabic-seed-014: A female student: the same word with ة at the end.
